source.quote: On November 14th, 2025, we notified developers using DALL·E model snapshots of their deprecation and removal from the API on May 12, 2026.

tasks.reasoning:
The realtime voice service pins gpt-4o-realtime-preview. The source says realtime preview models were removed on May 7, 2026 and the Realtime beta header on May 12, 2026. Both dates have passed, so the voice feature is already failing to connect. Migrate to gpt-realtime-2.1 or gpt-realtime-2.1-mini. Drop the OpenAI-Beta header and update the session.update and event shapes to the GA schema. The migration agent should check for the beta header and for event names like response.audio.delta that the GA API changed.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- openai:2026-07-20-legacy-audio-realtime (model-retirement): Legacy gpt-realtime, gpt-audio, mini and 4o audio/realtime models removed Jan 20, 2027; migrate to gpt-realtime-2.1 / gpt-realtime-2.1-mini / gpt-audio-1.5, effective 2027-01-20. That change removes the gpt-4o-realtime / gpt-realtime family on 2027-01-20. If this migration moves the realtime session straight to gpt-realtime-2.1 (or gpt-realtime-2.1-mini) and the GA interface, it avoids that retirement too and needs no second edit. Do not migrate to plain gpt-realtime.
  Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.md
  "On July 20, 2026, we notified developers using legacy audio, realtime, and transcription model families and snapshots of their deprecation and removal from the API on January 20, 2027."

callSites.why: The pinned model constant is gpt-4o-realtime-preview, which was removed on 2026-05-07.

Opens wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime with the removed preview model. It very likely sends the OpenAI-Beta: realtime=v1 header, which was removed on 2026-05-12, so the connection and session events must move to the GA Realtime interface.

## dall-e-2/dall-e-3 and Realtime beta header removed May 12, 2026; realtime preview/audio-preview models May 7, 2026 [Verified]

### Change

Moved the realtime voice proxy from gpt-4o-realtime-preview to gpt-realtime-2.1 on the GA interface. Removed the OpenAI-Beta header. session.update now uses the GA shape (type 'realtime', output_modalities ['audio'], audio.output.voice). The audio handler now listens for response.output_audio.delta. Updated docs. Added a mocked-ws jest test. Because it targets gpt-realtime-2.1, it also avoids the 2027-01-20 legacy realtime removal. No DALL-E or audio-preview usage was found in the repo.

Files touched:
- `docs/NESTJS_REALTIME_VOICE.md`
- `src/realtime/realtime-voice.service.spec.ts`
- `src/realtime/realtime-voice.service.ts`

### Why

gpt-4o-realtime-preview and the Realtime beta header were removed in May 2026, and the old session and event shapes differ in GA.

> On November 14th, 2025, we notified developers using DALL·E model snapshots of their deprecation and removal from the API on May 12, 2026.

Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | pass | pass | 0 |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| test | pass | pass | 0 |
| realtime-test | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- realtime-test, added by the agent: `export MONGO_URI='mongodb://user:pass@localhost:27017/db' JWT_SECRET='placeholder'; npx jest src/realtime` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Prepared before the baseline:
- Checks ran with placeholder env: MONGO_URI, JWT_SECRET.

Test of this change: `realtime-test`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- GA session.update schema and event names were taken from memory, not checked against the live docs or a live session
- Input audio format and turn-detection defaults were not set explicitly; GA defaults may differ from the beta ones (e.g. PCM16 24kHz)
- The gateway and the Flutter client were not reviewed for the output audio format
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- Model changes to gpt-realtime-2.1, so voice quality, latency and cost may differ
- Server audio events are now response.output_audio.delta (was response.audio.delta)
- The voice is set at session.audio.output.voice

review.summary: The diff covers the one named call site (src/realtime/realtime-voice.service.ts). It removes the `OpenAI-Beta: realtime=v1` header, moves the session.update payload to the GA shape (`type: 'realtime'`, `audio.output.voice`) and renames the audio delta event to `response.output_audio.delta`. That matches the GA migration as I understand it. Three things keep me from fully trusting the 'verified' grade. First, I could not confirm the model id `gpt-realtime-2.1`; the GA model I know is `gpt-realtime`, so this needs checking against current docs. Second, the only proof is a new spec that mocks `ws`, so nothing exercises the live server's acceptance of the URL, session payload or event names. Third, `output_modalities: ['audio']` is new behaviour that leaves the `onTextDelta` path effectively dead.

concerns.issue: Line 4: the model id `gpt-realtime-2.1` could not be confirmed from my knowledge or the quoted deprecation source. If the id doesn't exist, the WebSocket handshake or the session will fail at runtime. Every check passes regardless, because the spec only asserts the URL string it was written to match. Verify the id on the OpenAI models page or in the deprecations doc's replacement table (likely `gpt-realtime`).

The test fully mocks `ws` and asserts the exact payload the diff writes, so it is self-confirming. It does not prove the GA server accepts the session.update (GA rejects unknown or misplaced fields) or that `response.output_audio.delta` is what the server actually emits. The realtime-test 'before fail' is simply this new spec failing against old code; it is not an independent signal. With no live or recorded-fixture check, 'verified' overstates the evidence. needs-review fits better.

Line ~37: adding `output_modalities: ['audio']` is beyond what the migration forces. With audio-only output, GA sends the transcript as `response.output_audio_transcript.delta`, not `response.output_text.delta`, so the `onTextDelta` handler at ~line 53 will never fire. It was probably already dead under beta, where the event was `response.audio_transcript.delta`. Either listen for the transcript event or drop the claim from the docs.

The GA session no longer accepts flat `input_audio_format`/`turn_detection`, and its defaults may differ from beta's. The code relies on defaults: PCM16 24 kHz input and server VAD, while `commitAndCreateResponse` also commits manually. If GA's default turn detection is server_vad, a manual commit plus `response.create` can produce empty-buffer errors or duplicate responses. Consider setting `audio.input.format` and `turn_detection` explicitly.

Section 5 still lists `response.audio.delta` as the event the server sends the client. That is fine if src/realtime/realtime.gateway.ts wraps the deltas in its own envelope, but the gateway isn't shown, so confirm it doesn't forward raw OpenAI event types to the Flutter client.
The change notice also covers DALL·E 2/3 removal. The match agent named no images call sites; a quick grep for `dall-e` or `images.generate` would confirm nothing else is affected.

review.summary: The core change is handled: the Dockerfile moves both stages to node:22-alpine, package.json adds engines >=22, and openai is bumped to ^7.49.0. Typecheck passes against all 11 named chat.completions.create call sites, so their shapes still compile. The checks do not prove that the Docker image builds or runs on node:22-alpine, or that other deployment targets (CI, k8s, compose) also moved off Node 20. The lockfile also shows side effects that look like a regeneration with a different npm or peer resolution, not changes the bump requires. A real API call was never made. 'verified' is defensible for compile and unit level, but a human should check the points below before merging.

concerns.issue: openai 7.49.0 declares optional peer ws ^8.21.0, but package.json pins ws ^8.19.0 and the lockfile diff shows no ws change. If the locked ws is below 8.21, npm ci may fail with ERESOLVE or install with an invalid peer. Check the same for google-auth-library (peer >=9.15.1, package.json ^9.14.0).

Only the Dockerfile base image was bumped, and no check builds the image. The repo has k8s scripts (scripts/k8s/*), docker-compose files and possibly CI workflows, .nvmrc or a PaaS config that may still pin Node 20. With engines >=22 and openai requiring Node 22, any of those left on 20 will break. Native deps such as bcrypt@5 also need to install cleanly on node:22-alpine under `npm ci --omit=dev`.

Changes not caused by the bump: optional peer entries were dropped (mongoose's gaxios, gcp-metadata, node-fetch, https-proxy-agent, socks, smart-buffer, fetch-blob, etc.), and handlebars, minimist, neo-async, uglify-js and wordwrap became dev-only. These will be omitted from the production image by `npm ci --omit=dev`. That is harmless if nothing at runtime requires them (e.g. no handlebars email templates and no MongoDB KMS/SOCKS use), but it should be confirmed.

I could not confirm from the quoted source that openai 7.49.0 exists or that 7.x has no breaking changes beyond the Node 22 requirement. The `bin`/CLI entry is gone in the new lock entry. Check the full 7.0.0 changelog and the npm registry.

The test only checks the installed version, the Node version and the request body through a mocked fetch. It does not exercise the repo's own services (timeouts, response_format, error handling) or a live request. The Node >=22 assertion will also fail on any developer or CI machine still on Node 20, which may be intended. It reads node_modules relative to the current working directory, so it is fragile if jest runs from another directory.

checkFirst: Check the locked ws and google-auth-library versions in package-lock.json against openai 7's peer ranges (ws ^8.21.0, google-auth-library >=9.15.1).
Run `docker build .`, start the container on node:22-alpine and make one real chat.completions.create call (e.g. through AiService).
Search the repo for other Node version pins (.github/workflows, .nvmrc, k8s manifests, docker-compose*, PaaS config) and bump them to 22.
Read the openai-node 7.0.0 CHANGELOG entries beyond the Node 22 line for other breaking changes.

preparation.reasoning: Standard NestJS project with no codegen, no postinstall/prepare scripts, and no workspace packages. tsc, nest build and jest run directly after install. Only placeholder env vars are provided in case modules read them at load time.

review.summary: The diff swaps every hard-coded `gpt-4o-mini` default for `gpt-6-luna` at all 11 named call sites. It also does things the retirement does not force: it removes `temperature` in three services and renames `max_tokens` to `max_completion_tokens`. None of the checks makes a live call. So the new model ID, its parameter support and its output behaviour are unproven. Deployments that set `OPENAI_MODEL` (as `.env.example` suggests) keep using the retired model regardless of this change. The `verified` grade overstates what typecheck/build/tests plus a regex spec show; this reads as needs-review.

concerns.issue: Every call site reads `OPENAI_MODEL` / `OPENAI_SUGGESTION_MODEL` / `OPENAI_NOTIFICATION_MODEL` first and only falls back to the literal. Any Railway or production environment that already sets `OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini` (the old `.env.example` value) still calls the retired model after Jan 14, 2027. The code change does nothing for those deployments. The PR needs an explicit ops step to update the deployed env vars.

`temperature: 0.2` was removed, and the same happens in task-assignment-llm.service.ts (0.15) and proposal-plan-generator.service.ts (0.2). This changes output determinism for e-mail generation, task assignment and sprint planning. It is only justified if gpt-6-luna rejects `temperature`, and I could not confirm that. The PR is also inconsistent: the spec only polices `max_tokens`, so any `temperature` still passed in meeting.service.ts, market-intelligence.service.ts or the assistant clients (not shown in the diff) was left in place. Either the model accepts temperature and the removals are unnecessary, or it rejects it and those other sites will fail at runtime.

If gpt-6-luna is a reasoning-style model, `max_completion_tokens` also counts hidden reasoning tokens. Capping at 2048 (and 4096 in task-assignment and proposal-plan) could leave `content` empty. That throws 'Réponse OpenAI vide' and silently drops to fallbacks or null assignments. No test exercises this.
The call still sends `response_format: { type: 'json_object' }`. I could not confirm gpt-6-luna supports it. Check the deprecation page and the installed `openai` SDK types/model docs.

The guard test is weak. It only catches `'gpt-4o'` in single quotes, so double-quoted or template literals slip through. It skips every path containing 'realtime', so any retired gpt-4o realtime or other snapshot there is unchecked. It does not look at .env or docs. It does not check `temperature` at all. Its passing is what flipped 'model-spec' to pass, and it proves only the absence of strings.

Four call sites (574/656/755/937) had only their model default changed. Their request bodies are not shown, so I could not tell whether they pass parameters gpt-6-luna may not accept. Nothing in the diff or the checks shows these calls work with the new model.

checkFirst: Confirm `gpt-6-luna` is the documented replacement in https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.md. Confirm whether it accepts `temperature`, `max_tokens`/`max_completion_tokens` and `response_format: json_object`.
Update `OPENAI_MODEL`, `OPENAI_SUGGESTION_MODEL` and `OPENAI_NOTIFICATION_MODEL` in Railway/production. The code defaults are bypassed whenever these are set.

Grep meeting.service.ts, market-intelligence.service.ts, openai-notification.client.ts and openai-suggestion.client.ts for `temperature` and other sampling params. Handle them the same way as the three services the diff changed.
Run one live request per call site against gpt-6-luna, especially dispatch-email with the 2048-token cap. Confirm the content is non-empty and the JSON parses.
Search docs and other non-.ts files for remaining `gpt-4o` / `gpt-4.1` references, and check the 'realtime'-excluded paths for retired models.

review.summary: The PR does not address the stated change. The notice retires the transcription models `whisper-1`, `gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe` and `gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize`, plus `/v1/audio/translations`. The only named call site, `src/realtime/realtime-voice.service.ts`, uses none of these: it opens a Realtime session on `gpt-4o-realtime-preview` and configures no `input_audio_transcription`. Instead the diff migrates that file from the beta Realtime API to a GA-style session shape. That is a separate migration, and it changes behaviour, notably making the `onTextDelta` path dead. The model `gpt-realtime-2.1` could not be confirmed from the quoted source. The checks only exercise a mocked `ws`, so `verified` overstates what was proven.

concerns.issue: Out of scope for the transcription retirement. The original file never references `whisper-1`, the gpt-4o-*-transcribe models, `/v1/audio/transcriptions` or `/v1/audio/translations`. The beta-to-GA Realtime rewrite (URL model, removal of the `OpenAI-Beta` header, new session schema, renamed event) is a different API change and should be justified by its own source, or split into a separate PR.

`output_modalities: ['audio']` (new session block, around lines 36-37) restricts output to audio only. The existing handler still listens for `response.output_text.delta` to drive `onTextDelta`, and audio-only responses will not emit text deltas. The GA spoken-response transcript arrives as `response.output_audio_transcript.delta`. Callers that pass `onTextDelta` silently stop receiving text, a behaviour change the API change does not force.

Model `gpt-realtime-2.1` in `OPENAI_REALTIME_URL` (line 4) is not mentioned in the quoted deprecation text. I could not confirm it exists or is GA. Check the OpenAI models page and the Realtime GA docs. The fields `session.type: 'realtime'`, `audio.input/output.format {type:'audio/pcm', rate:24000}` and `audio.output.voice` should also be confirmed against the current Realtime session schema or the SDK types.

The new test mocks `ws` entirely. It asserts only that the code sends the payload it was written to send, not that OpenAI accepts it. No live session is opened, and nothing verifies that `sendAudioChunk` and `commitAndCreateResponse` (`input_audio_buffer.*`, `response.create`) still work under GA. The `realtime-proof` pass likely reflects this mock rather than a real call. A grade of `needs-review` would fit the evidence better than `verified`.

If the repo does use `whisper-1` or the gpt-4o transcribe models elsewhere, those call sites are untouched. Examples would be an `audio.transcriptions.create` call, a `/v1/audio/translations` call, or `input_audio_transcription` in another session. The match agent named only the realtime WebSocket, which suggests the real affected code may have been missed, or that this repo is not affected at all.

Run one live Realtime session (connect, append audio, commit, receive audio deltas) before treating this as verified.
